draft.title: Neurotransmitters at the synapse
card: A synapse is the tiny gap between two neurons. A neuron sends a message across it by releasing chemicals called neurotransmitters.
The neurotransmitters cross the synaptic gap and attach to receptors on the next neuron. A receptor only responds to neurotransmitters that fit it.
a neurotransmitter that makes the next neuron more likely to fire. Glutamate is an example.
a neurotransmitter that makes the next neuron less likely to fire. GABA is an example.
draft.remember: Neurotransmitters cross the gap and attach to receptors. Glutamate excites and GABA inhibits.

a.q: What is the effect when GABA attaches to receptors on the next neuron?
opts: The neuron becomes less likely to fire
The neuron becomes more likely to fire
The neuron becomes unable to release anything
The neuron becomes unable to receive anything
a.why: GABA is inhibitory, so it makes the receiving neuron less likely to fire. Glutamate is the one that makes a neuron more likely to fire, so the second option mixes the two up.

b.q: A drug blocks the glutamate receptors on neurons in one brain region. Glutamate is still released as normal. What is the most likely effect on those neurons?
opts: They are less likely to fire
They are more likely to fire
They are just as likely to fire as before
They are more likely to be inhibited by glutamate
b.why: Glutamate is excitatory, but it only has an effect when it attaches to receptors. With the receptors blocked, the neurons lose that excitatory input, so they are less likely to fire. Glutamate crossing the gap is not enough on its own.
b.clue: A neurotransmitter needs a receptor to attach to before it can act.

a.best: The neuron becomes less likely to fire

b.best: They are less likely to fire

problems.detail: The card defines the synapse as 'the tiny gap between two neurons'. The VCE Study Design treats the synapse as the whole junction: the presynaptic axon terminal, the synaptic gap and the postsynaptic membrane. The gap is only the synaptic gap, a term the card then uses separately, so the two are conflated.

check.summary: Both questions are sound and the explanations match the card. The one problem is that the card wrongly defines the synapse as just the gap between neurons; the VCE treats it as the whole junction, which includes the synaptic gap.
